title: Spanwise scratch trimming and kernel-padding optimizer to reduce transient GPU workspace
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU transient workspace up to 28% on long-context workloads via spanwise trimming and kernel padding heuristic; improves continuous-batching tail latency and reduces KV-cache eviction pressure.
description: Motivation: long-context generation and mixed-length continuous batching cause transient workspace blowups in the serving runtime. This PR introduces a spanwise scratch trimming pass plus a kernel-padding optimizer that cooperates with the scheduler and KV-cache pipeline to reduce peak ephemeral allocations without regressing throughput. High level: 1) Spanwise trimming: we analyze activation lifetimes at the operator-span level and release non-essential scratch segments earlier when safe (configurable slack). 2) Kernel-padding optimizer: a lightweight heuristic that chooses per-kernel padded workspace sizes to avoid pathological oversubscription from worst-case kernel footprints while still benefiting from vectorized kernels. 3) Scheduler hooks: new stride-aware scheduling hints let the batch coalescer and kernel launcher align padded sizes and avoid tail allocations. 4) KV-cache cooperation: a small API to allow the KV manager to proactively compact hot segments when a trimming window is entered. 5) Ops and ABI: additions are backwards-compatible; new options are gated behind runtime flags. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (internal/ENG-9341) - [x] unit tests for trimming heuristics - [x] integration test with continuous-batcher - [x] perf benches across long/short context mixes - [x] canary rollout plan and rollback flag Implementation notes: trimming introduces a conservative default slack of 8 tokens and is enabled for models with >8 layers by default; kernel-padding optimizer uses historical kernel footprint histograms collected during warmup to pick 75th-percentile padded sizes. Behavioural guarantees: no activation correctness changes; trimming only affects ephemeral scratch, not persistent checkpoints. Observability: added metrics runtime.scratch.trimmed_bytes, runtime.kernel.pad_factor, runtime.kv.compactions_triggered and traces for trimming windows. Rollout: feature is behind runtime flag redwood.runtime.span_trim_enable and will be enabled in Dedicated canaries for 48h before global rollout. Related: this complements ENG-9143 (arena tuning) and ENG-9410 (continuous batching improvements). Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9341/spanwise-scratch-trimming; canary run notes: internal/perf/canary-2024-11-10. Why different from previous work: instead of coarse arena-level free coalescing we operate at operator-span granularity and coordinate padded kernel sizing with the scheduler to avoid reintroducing fragmentation. CI: initial CI run failed on an unrelated Python lint in infra; fix was applied and CI green on rerun. Merge notes: squash merge after approvals; no migration scripts required.

review_comments: Aisha Khan: Nice direction; can you clarify how trimming interacts with checkpointing? Are we at risk of evicting live activation slices?

Priya Nair: Trimming only targets scratch buffers allocated by kernels (transient workspaces). Persistent activation checkpoints are untouched. We added assertions in debug builds to ensure no overlap with checkpoint allocations.
Marco Li: CI flaky in integration test on GPU memory error during initial run; looks like a race in KV compactor. Can you add a backoff?
Priya Nair: Added a linear backoff and a retry in kv_compactor; updated tests to surface retries deterministically. Reran canary and memory error did not reproduce.
Daniel Reiser: Request changes on observable labels — prefer runtime.kernel.pad_factor -> runtime.kernel.pad_ratio for consistency across metrics
Priya Nair: Renamed metric in latest commit and updated dashboards in docs link.
